# Scene encoders: point-based networks

<!-- slot-head:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->
<div class="gp-chips"><span class="gp-chip">Seed-based · 5 methods</span><code class="gp-chip">--set backbone=</code><span class="gp-chip">23 options</span></div>
<!-- slot-head:end -->

These encoders work on the raw point cloud: set abstraction (PointNet++ and its descendants),
residual MLPs, graph convolutions and random sampling. Their radii and neighbour counts set how
far a point sees. What all scene encoders share is on the [overview](scene_encoders.md).

## Use it

<!-- method-options:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->

=== "GraspNet-baseline"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set backbone=pointnext -o graspnet-baseline_pointnext.yaml
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e --list backbone
    ```

=== "GSNet"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set backbone=pointnext -o gsnet_pointnext.yaml
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list backbone
    ```

=== "Scale-Balanced-Grasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set backbone=pointnext -o scale-balanced-grasp_pointnext.yaml
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e --list backbone
    ```

=== "EconomicGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set backbone=pointnext -o economicgrasp_pointnext.yaml
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list backbone
    ```

=== "FineGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set backbone=pointnext -o finegrasp_pointnext.yaml
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list backbone
    ```

The first command writes a checked config; the second lists every option of the slot under that method, with what was measured. Then `grasppanda probe <file>` tries the config on real frames and `grasppanda train <file>` trains it ([Swap a component](../get_started/swap.md)). Each method page lists the same: [GraspNet-baseline](../methods/graspnet_baseline.md#backbone) · [GSNet](../methods/gsnet.md#backbone) · [Scale-Balanced-Grasp](../methods/scale_balanced_grasp.md#backbone) · [EconomicGrasp](../methods/economicgrasp.md#backbone) · [FineGrasp](../methods/finegrasp.md#backbone).

<!-- method-options:end -->

## Choosing

- **The PointNet++ family of the ported methods:** `pointnet2` and `pointnet2-transformer`;
  `-dense` propagates features back to every point, `-msg` uses two balls per level.
- **Modern set abstraction:** `pointnext` in four sizes, `pointmetabase` (one ball query per
  stage, the cheapest of them) and `pointvector`.
- **Full resolution, no sub-sampling:** `dgcnn` and the `pyg-*` layers; memory grows with the
  number of points times the neighbours.
- **Cheap sampling:** `randlanet` samples at random and pools attentively.
- **Radii are set for a table top by analogy.** The published configurations are for rooms
  (first radius 0.1 m); sweep the radius before comparing encoders.

## Details

??? note "The settings that matter, encoder by encoder"

    Options are changed with `--opts model.backbone.<option>=<value>`; the path addresses the
    encoder wherever an adapter put it.

    **PointNet++ with multi-scale grouping** (`pointnet2-msg`, `pointnet2-msg-dense`):

    ```yaml
    model:
      backbone:
        type: PointNet2MSG
        in_channels: 0
        npoints: [2048, 1024, 512, 256]
        radii: [[0.02, 0.04], [0.05, 0.1], [0.1, 0.2], [0.2, 0.3]]    # one list per level
        nsamples: [[32, 64], [16, 32], [16, 16], [16, 16]]
    ```

    `PointNet2MSG` keeps the level sizes of GraspNet-baseline (1024 seeds, 256 channels) with two
    balls per level; the larger ball is what a single-scale network would use, the smaller helps
    where points are dense. Cost grows with the sum of `nsamples` over the scales.

    **PointNeXt sizes**:

    | Preset | `blocks` | `width` | `sa_layers` / `sa_use_res` | Parameters with the official segmentation head |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | `pointnext` (S) | 1, 1, 1, 1, 1 | 32 | 2 / true | 0.792 M |
    | `pointnext-b` | 1, 2, 3, 2, 2 | 32 | 1 / false | 3.828 M |
    | `pointnext-l` | 1, 3, 5, 3, 3 | 32 | 1 / false | 7.125 M |
    | `pointnext-xl` | 1, 4, 7, 4, 4 | 64 | 1 / false | 41.576 M |

    The presets set `radius: 0.04` (the room value is 0.1). Every inverted residual block runs
    one ball query.

    **PointMetaBase and PointVector** take the arguments of `PointNeXt` (`blocks`, `width`,
    `strides`, `radius`, `nsample`). PointMetaBase shares one ball query and one offset embedding
    per stage; the unit suite pins its sizes to the published ones. PointVector is the scene
    network of the official code. Their output width is `width` (32 or 64).

    **ASSANet**: `use_xyz: true` (set by the preset) appends the coordinates to the input
    features. Without it, constant input features are normalised to zero and the encoder learns
    nothing; the class refuses that combination in training.

    **PointMLP**: neighbourhoods by count, anchors by ratio, so nothing to convert from rooms.
    `gmp_dim` appends a max-pooled vector of the whole frame to every point (0 turns it off).

    **DeLA**: `grid_size[0]` is the spacing of the input cloud and sets the unit of the offset
    encoding; keep the factor of 2 between levels unless you also change `k`. Level sizes depend
    on the frame, so DeLA is `dense` only.

    **DGCNN**: `k` neighbours per point; `dynamic: true` rebuilds the graph in feature space
    (the paper), `false` keeps it spatial; `emb_dims` is the width of the frame-level vector (0
    leaves it out). Keep `coords_as_features: true` with constant input features.

    **RandLA-Net**: `sub_sampling_ratio` and `dim_output` per level. Sampling is random in
    training and a fixed permutation in evaluation, so inference is repeatable. A cloud needs at
    least `num_neighbors × prod(ratios[:-1])` points.

    **PyTorch Geometric layers** (extra `torch_geometric`): a stack of one library convolution
    at full resolution; only the layers are the library's, the stack is not a published network.

    | Preset | `conv` | Library layer |
    |---|---|---|
    | `pyg-pointnet` | `pointnet` | `torch_geometric.nn.PointNetConv` |
    | `pyg-edgeconv` | `edge` | `torch_geometric.nn.EdgeConv` |
    | `pyg-point-transformer` | `point_transformer` | `torch_geometric.nn.PointTransformerConv` |
    | `pyg-pointgnn` | `pointgnn` | `torch_geometric.nn.PointGNNConv` (all `channels` equal) |

??? note "Released weights for PointNet++ and PointNeXt"

    `tools/convert_backbone_weights.py` cuts the encoder out of a released checkpoint, checks it
    strictly against the class and writes a file whose keys start with `backbone.`. Nothing is
    downloaded by the tool.

    <div data-search-exclude markdown>

    | `--format` | Source file | Fits | Trained on | Licence | SHA-256, first 16 |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | `pointnext-s` (`-b`, `-l`, `-xl`) | the S3DIS checkpoints linked from [PointNeXt `docs/modelzoo.md`](https://github.com/guochengqian/PointNeXt/blob/master/docs/modelzoo.md) | `PointNeXt(in_channels=4, ...)` of that size | S3DIS area 5, rooms at 4 cm, colour + height | code MIT; weights not stated | S (9.6 MB): `95802f5c110e9fdd`; B, L, XL not downloaded |
    | `votenet` | the files of `votenet_pretrained_models.zip` linked from the [VoteNet README](https://github.com/facebookresearch/votenet) | `PointNet2(in_channels=1, radii=[0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1.2])` | SUN RGB-D single-view scans; ScanNet | code MIT; weights not stated | SUN RGB-D: `ff645ce392676cc4`; ScanNet: `22e57a2b8df1315a` (11.5 MB each) |
    | `csc-pointnet2`, `csc-pointnet2-dense` | the PointNet++ pre-training linked from the [Contrastive Scene Contexts README](https://github.com/facebookresearch/ContrastiveSceneContexts) | `PointNet2` (the GraspNet-baseline layout) or `PointNet2Dense`, coordinates only | ScanNet frame pairs, self-supervised | code MIT; weights not stated | `a6812612720295ff` (6.4 MB) |

    </div>

    The checksums are those of the files as downloaded on 2026-10-13; the full digests are in
    `tests/integration/test_backbone_released_weights.py`, which checks them before it loads a
    file.

    ```bash
    python -m tools.convert_backbone_weights --list
    python -m tools.convert_backbone_weights partition8_4096_15k_pointnet.pth csc_pointnet2.pth \
        --format csc-pointnet2
    grasppanda train <method config> \
        --opts runtime.load_from=csc_pointnet2.pth runtime.allow_weight_mismatch=true
    ```

    - **Radii are not stored in a checkpoint.** These networks were trained with room radii;
      they load under table-top radii without complaint, and then see the table enlarged about
      five times. Whether that helps is untested.
    - **Input channels are part of the weights.** PointNeXt reads colour and a height above the
      floor, VoteNet one height channel; a camera-frame table-top cloud has no floor height, so
      define what you feed.
    - The dataset terms of S3DIS, SUN RGB-D and ScanNet apply; treat the files as research-only
      until you have checked. The files were loaded strictly once; activations were not compared
      with the upstream code.

??? warning "Pitfalls met while building this"

    - **The grouper of Scale-Balanced-Grasp wants 256 channels.** `pointnext*`,
      `pointmetabase*` and `pointvector*` end on 32 or 64; compose puts the projected grouper in
      place, and the model is then a variant of Scale-Balanced-Grasp. The encoders whose width
      is free are set 256 wide by their presets for this reason.
    - **Constant input features starve encoders that read geometry through features.** `DGCNN`,
      `PyGPointEncoder`, `RandLANet` and `PointMLP` therefore read the coordinates themselves.
    - **Absolute coordinates.** RandLA-Net's neighbourhood encoding, DGCNN, PointMLP and the
      bridge read camera-frame coordinates as features, so their features are not translation
      invariant.
    - **Frame-level vectors.** `dgcnn` (`emb_dims`) and `pointmlp` (`gmp_dim`) append a vector of
      the whole frame to every point, so features depend on the workspace crop; both can be
      switched off.
    - **Padded balls under mean or sum.** A ball query pads a sparse ball by repeating its first
      hit; `assanet` (mean) and `pointvector` (sum) count it several times, as upstream does.
    - **`torch_geometric` without `pyg-lib`** cannot build a k-NN graph; the bridge builds it
      itself.

??? note "Not wrapped"

    | Candidate | Why not |
    |---|---|
    | KPConv (rigid and deformable) | needs kernel-point dispositions, radius neighbourhoods and a grid pyramid computed in its own data pipeline with compiled code; a follow-up of its own. |
    | KPConvX / KPConvD | expected to need the same; not attempted. |
    | RandLA-Net, authors' repository | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; the MIT implementation of Open3D-ML was adapted instead. |
    | Contact-GraspNet's PointNet++ layout and weights | a non-commercial licence; its three-scale layout can be written as a `PointNet2MSG` config by hand. |
    | `XConv` (PointCNN), `GravNetConv` of PyTorch Geometric | they build their graph inside the layer, which needs `pyg-lib`. |
    | DeepLA-Net, LinNet, PointMixer, SPoTr, X-3D, PAConv, RepSurf, PVCNN, DeepGCN | not reached, or no licence file found earlier. |
